בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר נָתַן לַשֶּׂכְוִי בִינָה לְהַבְחִין בֵּין יוֹם וּבֵין לָיְלָה׃
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא עָשַׂנִי נָכְרִי׃
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא עָשַׂנִי עָבֶד׃
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא עָשַׂנִי אִשָּׁה׃
In place of the preceding benediction women say:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם שֶׁעָשַׂנִי כִּרְצוֹנוֹ׃
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם פּוֹקֵחַ עִוְרִים׃
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם מַלְבִּישׁ עֲרֻמִּים׃
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם מַתִּיר אֲסוּרִים׃
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם זוֹקֵף כְּפוּפִים׃
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם רוֹקַע הָאָרֶץ עַל־הַמָּיִם׃
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם שֶׁעָשָׂה לִי כָּל־צָרְכִּי׃
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר הֵכִין מִצְעֲדֵי־גָבֶר׃
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם אוֹזֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּגְבוּרָה׃
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם עוֹטֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּתִפְאָרָה׃
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם הַנּוֹתֵן לַיָּעֵף כֹּחַ׃
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם הַמַּעֲבִיר שֵׁנָה מֵעֵינַי וּתְנוּמָה מֵעַפְעַפָּי׃

וִיהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁתַּרְגִּילֵנוּ בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ וְדַבְּקֵנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתֶיךָ וְאַל תְּבִיאֵנוּ לֹא לִידֵי חֵטְא וְלֹא לִידֵי עֲבֵרָה וְעָוֹן וְלֹא לִידֵי נִסָּיוֹן וְלֹא לִידֵי בִזָּיוֹן וְאַל תַּשְׁלֶט בָּנוּ יֵצֶר הָרָע וְהַרְחִיקֵנוּ מֵאָדָם רָע וּמֵחָבֵר רָע וְדַבְּקֵנוּ בְּיֵצֶר הַטּוֹב וּבְמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים וְכֹף אֶת יִצְרֵנוּ [continues on p. 7]
6 Morning Prayer 6
ברוך
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who gave the cock the capacity to distinguish between day and night.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who did not make me a non-Jew.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who did not make me a slave.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who did not make me a woman.
In place of the preceding benediction women say:
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who made me according to His will.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who made me according to His will.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who makes the blind see.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who clothes the naked.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who frees the bound.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who makes the bent erect.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who extends the earth above the water.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who made for me all that I need.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who makes man's steps firm.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who girds Israel with might.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who crowns Israel with splendour.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who gives strength to the weary.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who removes sleep from my eyes and slumber from my eyelids.
ויהי

May it be Thy will, O Lord our God and God of our fathers, to make us regular in the study of Thy Torah, and to make us adhere to Thy commandments. Let us not come to sin, transgression and guilt, nor to temptation, nor to shame. Let not the evil inclination rule over us. Keep us far from wicked people, from evil companions. Let us adhere to [continues on p. 7]
7 תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית 7

[continued from p. 6] לְהִשְׁתַּעְבֶּד־לָךְ וּתְנֵנוּ הַיּוֹם וּבְכָל־יוֹם לְחֵן וּלְחֶסֶד וּלְרַחֲמִים בְּעֵינֶיךָ וּבְעֵינֵי כָל־רוֹאֵינוּ וְתִגְמְלֵנוּ חֲסָדִים טוֹבִים. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ גּוֹמֵל חֲסָדִים טוֹבִים לְעַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל׃

יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהַי וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתַי שֶׁתַּצִּילֵנִי הַיּוֹם וּבְכָל־יוֹם מֵעַזֵּי פָנִים וּמֵעַזּוּת פָּנִים מֵאָדָם רָע וּמֵחָבֵר רָע וּמִשָּׁכֵן רָע וּמִפֶּגַע רָע וּמִשָּׂטָן הַמַּשְׁחִית מִדִּין קָשֶׁה וּמִבַּעַל דִּין קָשֶׁה בֵּין שֶׁהוּא בֶּן־בְּרִית וּבֵין שֶׁאֵינוֹ בֶן־בְּרִית׃
לְעוֹלָם יְהֵא אָדָם יְרֵא שָׁמַיִם בְּסֵתֶר וּמוֹדֶה עַל־הָאֱמֶת וְדוֹבֵר אֱמֶת בִּלְבָבוֹ וְיַשְׁכֵּם וְיֹאמַר׃

רִבּוֹן כָּל־הָעוֹלָמִים לֹא עַל־צִדְקוֹתֵינוּ אֲנַחְנוּ מַפִּילִים תַּחֲנוּנֵינוּ לְפָנֶיךָ כִּי עַל רַחֲמֶיךָ הָרַבִּים. מָה אֲנַחְנוּ מֶה חַיֵּינוּ מֶה חַסְדֵּנוּ מַה־צִּדְקוֹתֵינוּ מַה־יְשׁוּעָתֵנוּ מַה־כֹּחֵנוּ מַה־גְּבוּרָתֵנוּ מַה־נֹּאמַר לְפָנֶיךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ הֲלֹא כָּל־הַגִּבּוֹרִים כְּאַיִן לְפָנֶיךָ וְאַנְשֵׁי הַשֵּׁם כְּלֹא הָיוּ וַחֲכָמִים כִּבְלִי מַדָּע וּנְבוֹנִים כִּבְלִי הַשְׂכֵּל כִּי רֹב מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם תֹּהוּ וִימֵי חַיֵּיהֶם הֶבֶל לְפָנֶיךָ. וּמוֹתַר הָאָדָם מִן־הַבְּהֵמָה אָיִן כִּי הַכֹּל הָבֶל׃

אֲבָל אֲנַחְנוּ עַמְּךָ בְּנֵי בְרִיתֶךָ. בְּנֵי אַבְרָהָם אֹהַבְךָ שֶׁנִּשְׁבַּעְתָּ לּוֹ בְּהַר הַמּוֹרִיָּה. זֶרַע יִצְחָק יְחִידוֹ שֶׁנֶּעֱקַד עַל גַּב־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ עֲדַת יַעֲקֹב בִּנְךָ בְּכוֹרֶךָ שֶׁמֵּאַהֲבָתְךָ שֶׁאָהַבְתָּ אֹתוֹ וּמִשִּׂמְחָתְךָ שֶׁשָּׂמַחְתָּ־בּוֹ קָרָאתָ אֶת־שְׁמוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל וִישֻׁרוּן׃
7 Morning Prayer 7

[continued from p. 6] the good inclination and good deeds, force our inclination to serve Thee; let us today and every day find favour, grace and compassion in Thine eyes and in the eyes of all who see us and bestow upon us kindnesses. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, who bestows kindnesses upon His people Israel.
יהי

May it be Thy will, O Lord my God and God of my fathers, to save me today and everyday from the impudent and from impudence, from evil men, from evil companions, from evil neighbours, from evil encounters, from Satan the destroyer, from a harsh verdict and from a harsh opponent, whether Jew or non-Jew.
לעולם
Let man always fear God in private, acknowledge the truth, speak truth in his heart and rise early in the morning and say:
רבון

Lord of all worlds! Not on account of our righteousness do we lay our supplications before Thee but because of Thy great compassion. What are we, what is our life, what is our grace, what is our righteousness, what is our aid, what is our power, what is our strength. What shall we speak before Thee, O Lord our God and God of our fathers, truly all heroes are as nothing before Thee, famous men as though they had never existed, wise men as though without understanding and intelligent people as though without sense; for the amount of their work is vain and the days of their lives are empty before Thee, and the superiority of man over the animal is nought for everything is vain.
אבל

But we are Thy people, children of Thy covenant, children of Abraham who loved Thee, whom Thou didst make a promise on Mount Moriah, the seed of Isaac, his only son, who was bound on the altar, the congregation of Jacob, Thy firstborn son, whose name, out of Thy love with which Thou didst love him, and out of Thy joy with which Thou didst rejoice in him, Thou hast called Israel and Yeshurun.

uncertainties: Scan resolution makes fine pointing hard to read with confidence; dagesh, hataf and holam marks especially should be checked against a higher-resolution image.
s48 line 2: there is a small stray dash or mark at the right edge just before לַשֶּׂכְוִי. It may be a print artifact or a broken maqaf. I left it out of the text.
s48: בִינָה looks like it has no dagesh in the bet (after לַשֶּׂכְוִי). I transcribed it as seen.
s48: I read מֵעֵינַי and מֵעַפְעַפָּי, but the final vowels (patah vs qamats, qamats vs hiriq) are not certain.
s48: עֲרֻמִּים, the qubuts and dagesh are not certain.
s48: I read תַּשְׁלֶט בָּנוּ with no visible maqaf. A maqaf may be there and too faint to see.
s48: כָּל־צָרְכִּי, I read the pointing as qamats under the tsade and dagesh in the kaf. Not certain.
s50: for the first פָנִים in מֵעַזֵּי פָנִים I can't tell whether the pe has a dagesh.
s50: וּמִשָּׁכֵן, the vowel under the shin (qamats vs sheva) is unclear.
s50: there is a small stray mark below and left of הַמַּשְׁחִית at the left margin, probably a print artifact.
s50: the first בֶּן־בְּרִית looks like it has a dagesh and the second בֶן־בְּרִית does not. Not certain.
s50: מַה־יְשׁוּעָתֵנוּ, I can't see a dagesh in the yod. In מַה־נֹּאמַר the dagesh is also uncertain.
s50: I read the word as רֹב in כִּי רֹב מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם, but it could be רַב. The image is not clear enough to decide.
s50: I can't tell whether לּוֹ in שֶׁנִּשְׁבַּעְתָּ לּוֹ has a dagesh. I also can't tell whether the word is spelled אֹתוֹ or אוֹתוֹ.
s50: in the small-type לְעוֹלָם paragraph the pointing (בְּסֵתֶר, וְיַשְׁכֵּם) is only partly legible.
observations: Apparent original duplicate (English, s49): the women's blessing 'Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who made me according to His will.' is printed twice. First it appears in small type under the instruction. Then it is repeated at full size as if it were a separate blessing, before 'who makes the blind see.' The Hebrew page (s48) prints שֶׁעָשַׂנִי כִּרְצוֹנוֹ only once, in small type. The full-size English repeat has no Hebrew counterpart and looks like a typesetting error.
The instruction 'In place of the preceding benediction women say:' is printed in English italics on both the Hebrew page and the English page.

Page boundary: the first Yehi Ratzon (וִיהִי רָצוֹן … שֶׁתַּרְגִּילֵנוּ) runs from Hebrew p. 6 onto p. 7. P. 6 ends at 'וְכֹף אֶת יִצְרֵנוּ' and p. 7 continues with 'לְהִשְׁתַּעְבֶּד־לָךְ'. The English does the same: p. 6 ends 'Let us adhere to' and p. 7 continues 'the good inclination…'.

Linkage cues on the English pages are Hebrew catchwords at the start of paragraphs: ברוך, ויהי, יהי, לעולם, רבון, אבל. There is only one ברוך cue, at the first blessing. The other English blessings have no cue.
The first English Yehi Ratzon cue is ויהי, which matches the Hebrew opening וִיהִי. The second is יהי, which matches יְהִי.
The לְעוֹלָם paragraph is in smaller, indented type on the Hebrew page and in indented italics on the English page. It works as an introduction to רִבּוֹן but is printed as text to be said.
Possible English typo: 'everyday' (one word) in 'to save me today and everyday' (s51).
Odd English wording kept as printed: 'whom Thou didst make a promise on Mount Moriah' (s51).
On Hebrew p. 7 several lines end with a dangling maqaf at the line break (מַה־ / כֹּחֵנוּ; אֶת־ / שְׁמוֹ). I joined them in the transcription.
Divine name is printed as יְיָ throughout.
The Hebrew running header on p. 6 has the page number on the left only. On p. 7 it has the page number on both sides.
